sources.entry: OFBiz - Enterprise Resource Planning system with a suite of business applications flexible enough to be used across any industry. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Apache OFBiz is an open-source Java ERP system with a large set of business applications, libraries, entities and services for running many aspects of a business.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OFBiz as an Enterprise Resource Planning system written in Java, bundling libraries, entities, services and features for running business operations. It names several back-office interfaces, including Order, Accounting and Administrator, reachable in a browser after startup. Build and run tasks are driven by an embedded Gradle wrapper, with commands for loading seed, demo and external data, running unit and integration tests, and creating tenants in multitenant setups. A plugin system lets components be pulled, installed, created and pushed from the plugins directory or a Maven repository. Production use is covered by building a tar or zip distribution and running bin/ofbiz, with options for an external database such as MySQL or PostgreSQL and Docker.
use_cases: running an ERP for a small or mid-sized business
managing orders and accounting in one system
self-hosting a Java business application suite
customizing ERP functionality through components or plugins
how_to_run: Run ./gradlew cleanAll loadAll (this deletes existing data and loads demo data)
Open the browser to the Order, Accounting or Administrator interface and log in as admin / ofbiz
notable: Embedded Gradle build with server-control tasks such as start, shutdown, status and background mode
Plugin system with pull, install, create and push tasks
Data loading by reader type (seed, seed-initial, demo, ext, ext-test) with fine-grained options
Multitenant support with tenant creation and per-tenant data loading
Split repositories: ofbiz-framework core and ofbiz-plugins for optional components
caveats: Requires JDK 17 and, on Windows, a PowerShell 7.1.3 or later and an install path without spaces
Initial setup needs an internet connection to download dependencies; offline use relies on a prior cache
The Windows ofbiz.bat script can fail with a 'input line is too long' error, with a workaround given
Default production deployment configuration is tied to the source code, per the README
